scope: Source-label length and Unicode code-point compatibility in durable search-history readback.
problem: The client applied a 200-UTF-16-unit limit to source labels while persistence supports up to 256 Python code points. A stored 201-character ASCII label could therefore invalidate the entire history page.
change: A source-specific guard preserves the existing nonempty/control checks, bounds input to 512 UTF-16 units, then requires at most 256 Unicode code points.
The returned source is preserved exactly. ID, profile, query, error, cursor and other record guards remain unchanged.

All seven original client cases remain; five focused cases cover 201/256 ASCII, 256 mixed Unicode, 257-code-point rejection and existing blank/control rejection. The original connected browser class remains unmodified and unselected.

metadata_commit.identity_binding: The containing Git/PR head binds these metadata bytes externally.

source_identity.interpretation: The baseline, fixed-web and browser executions used frozen uncommitted capsules and retain null candidate_commit. The later source commit has separately verified full-tree and three-blob equivalence. It does not change the identity under which the tests ran.

baseline.selected_case: preserves backend-valid source lengths: 201 ASCII code points

observed_assertion.name: AssertionError
observed_assertion.interpretation: The selected promise-resolution assertion rejects with the client INVALID_RESPONSE cause for a synthetic 201-code-point ASCII source label.
observed_assertion.display_limit: The rendered Vitest message is abbreviated; actual structured cause.name and cause.kind are retained without inventing omitted text.

fixed_browser.scope: The real record builder and SQLite persistence seeded four synthetic terminal history records before the read baseline. The compiled SPA used the local API and original browser-triggered GET responses; the test did not reissue or fulfill responses. No provider or discovery campaign was run.

requirement_scope.literal_requirement: Store: source, query, profile, filters, start, finish, results, new jobs, duplicates, errors.
requirement_scope.verified_slice: Preserve durable search-history source labels within the existing 256-code-point storage length limit in client parsing and connected browser readback.
requirement_scope.scope_boundary: Only source length and Unicode code-point compatibility changes. Existing JavaScript nonempty and C0/DEL rejection remain. Python strip and JavaScript trim differ, and persistence permits DEL; universal whitespace/control admission agreement is not claimed.
requirement_scope.outside_scope: API and storage code, ID/profile/query/error/cursor guards, provider discovery, campaigns, PREPARE/submission, and the remaining literal MJ236 criteria are outside this repair.

preserved_failed_attempts.cause: The new fixture referenced models.application_attempts, but the exported table object is models.attempts. AttributeError occurred before Playwright/browser startup.
preserved_failed_attempts.correction: One fixture symbol changed to models.attempts; models.operations was already valid. Production/client and unit-test bytes were preserved.

preserved_failed_attempts.cause: The copied reporter still targeted baseline-unit-01/vitest-run-end.json. Its exclusive wx write raised EEXIST; the required baseline-unit-02 run-end file was absent, causing downstream FileNotFoundError.
preserved_failed_attempts.raw_vitest_observation: The raw Vitest JSON contains one failed and eleven filtered cases, but reporter/tooling failure prevents baseline qualification.
preserved_failed_attempts.correction: A fresh baseline-unit-03 attempt used the corrected reporter destination and propagated byte pins. Normal qualification gates were unchanged.

earlier_qualified_proofs.interpretation: Earlier baseline01 and fixed-web01 remain evidence only for their original capsules; they are not relabeled as corrected-source or later-commit proof.

restoration02.interpretation: The client was restored to its original native CRLF bytes and the browser fixture symbol was corrected; the unit test was retained. This was a restoration transition, not a first test-only application.

preparation_and_attempt_history.fixed_reporter_preparation_correction: The analogous fixed-web reporter destination was corrected before fixed-web02 ran. The earlier static approval and corrective addendum are preserved; no qualification exception was introduced.

warnings.text: Some chunks are larger than 500 kB after minification.

runtime_limit.interpretation: The local unit/build results used the sealed Node 27 alpha environment. The browser consumed that compiled SPA. Hosted Node 24 checks and any protected-main integration remain separate.

artifact_path_basis: Artifact paths are relative to the retained run evidence root; repository paths are explicitly labeled.
limits: This proves the bounded source length/code-point repair and selected local readback behavior, not complete MJ236 acceptance.
Four synthetic history records were deliberately written before the browser read baseline; only the subsequent browser traffic and before/after database comparison are GET-only and unchanged.
No provider result, campaign, PREPARE/submission, hosted-check result, merge or deployment is claimed.
Protected-main changes do not retarget these base 0a84 / corrected 03b runtime proofs; final publication admission must separately bind its reviewed target.

execution_context.representation: Sanitized representations of recorded execution data. Defined native-root prefixes are replaced by placeholders; the arrays preserve argument order, flags and all other values. Placeholder paths are not literal executed paths or portable reproduction commands.

<RUN_ROOT>.meaning: Private immutable evidence root for this run_id. Artifact references in this document are relative to this root.

<REPOSITORY_ROOT>.meaning: Native repository root containing the recorded Python virtual environment.

<NODE_INSTALL_ROOT>.meaning: Native Node/npm installation root containing the recorded node.exe.

operating_system.basis: The qualified supervisor loads Windows kernel32 through ctypes.WinDLL and records native Windows Job accounting; the recorded Python build is MSC AMD64.

npm.role: Recorded toolchain identity from the qualified historical dependency installation reused by these phases; the selected validation commands invoke Node directly, not npm.

execution_context.timing_note: Each timestamp retains the meaning and field name of its raw receipt. Parent/child finished_at_utc fields are not substituted for the separately recorded final compute-release time. No missing outer-shell argv or pytest start timestamp is inferred.

sanitized_argv: preserves backend-valid source lengths: 201 ASCII code points$

creation_time_source.conversion: Exact conversion of Windows FILETIME 100 ns ticks since 1601-01-01 UTC; derived UTC rendering, not an independently recorded timestamp.

node_execution.result_interpretation: Node exit 1 is the selected expected behavioral failure; the normal qualified parent and child hosts exit 0.

pytest_execution.representation: Sanitized argument list passed to pytest.main inside the recorded Python child; this is not a separate python -m pytest subprocess.
pytest_execution.start_timestamp_status: NOT_SEPARATELY_RECORDED; child start above is not relabeled as pytest start.

execution_context.artifact_reference_basis: artifact_key values resolve to the pinned entries in /artifacts or the additional entries in /execution_context/artifacts. JSON pointers identify the exact original raw field.
